summary: diezyyasha-baileys ships char-code-obfuscated network host in messages-send
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. lib/Socket/messages-send.js contains a hidden network destination constructed via String.fromCharCode(...) at lines 425 and 436, which decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. Concealing an outbound host behind a decimal char-code array inside the message-send path — rather than as a plain string — is not consistent with normal library behavior; the same pattern is used by tampered Baileys forks to covertly relay message or session data through an author-controlled endpoint on top of the legitimate WhatsApp socket. Encoding the URL character-by-character has no benign purpose in a messaging library and hides the destination from casual source inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
